newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, trying again, makes Tenet his CIA nominee.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, trying again, makes Tenet his CIA nominee.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday nominated acting CIA Director George Tenet to be permanent chief of the spy agency, replacing nominee Anthony Lake who withdrew amid a rough Senate confirmation process.

"I want to announce my intention to nominate George Tenet as the director of central intelligence. He brings a wealth of experience and skill to the challege of leading our intelligence community into the 21st century," Clinton said in an announcement designed to put one big problem behind him before he left for a summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki, Finland.

"Mr. president, if confirmed I will do my level best to provide leadership, stability and strength of purpose to the men and women who serve our nation with such devotion" in the intelligence services, Tenet said in a statement he read at Clinton's invitation.

The nomination of Tenet, 44, who was deputy CIA director before interim appointment as acting director last December, was unlikely to spark the kind of stiff opposition that led Lake to give up his confirmation fight last Monday. Tenet has served as staff director of the Senate Intelligence Committee, which anchors the confirmation process, and was confirmed unanimously for the post of deputy CIA director in 1995.

In addition, as acting director, he is already overseeing the work of the Central Intelligence Agency and 12 other U.S. spy agencies said to employ about 80,000 people and spend about $30 billion a year among them. Questions about Lake's ability to manage that sprawling community helped thwart his confirmation.
Asked if he believed Tenet would be confirmed, Clinton replied, "I do," adding that his new nominee was "well known in the Senate, well respected by Republicans as well as Democrats."
